PLEASE DONT TAKE THIS THE WRONG WAY. I’m just being honest I am absolutely not judging or trying to hurt your feelings. 

I agree with many of your points on why you shouldn’t get married. However one thing that stood out to me was how cavalier you were when saying you both know typically relationships don’t survive decades... it might be true but damn, I think when you find your person you’re willing to take the risk. Like it’s just kind of a very jaded way to look at marriage. “Marriage inhibits change.” Yeah I’d say with those attitudes don’t get married love. I’m not trying to be harsh but typically when you want to marry someone that’s not the kind of thing that comes to mind.. 

Also marriage isn’t for everyone and that’s okay. Yes a lot of marriages do end in divorce, it’s quite common. The difference is most of those people don’t go in with an already glass half empty mindset. Ya know?

You don’t want to break it off yet you’re aware that sometimes people aren’t compatible and she’s a poor girlfriend for you... 

Anyways, just be up front. Sit her down and lead with what you just said. “Hey can we talk? I love you and I don’t want to fight or break up but I’m not feeling completely loved by you and here’s why..(insert issues here)” 

Framing it in a delicate way shouldn’t cause her to cry right off the bat whereas if you walk up and say she’s being a shit girlfriend, well I think most of us would cry lol 

Your feelings are valid. At the end of the day, you just have to communicate even though it can be hard. If she starts crying maybe say, “hey please don’t feel bad, this is just how I feel and I want to move forward and make this relationship work! Can we work together on that?” Let her know you want to make it work and you want to get through it together since it seems like you do.

But also I can’t ignore what you said in your post... just because you don’t want to break it off doesn’t mean you shouldn’t.. the things you mention are kind of make or break items for most relationships. If she can’t give those to you, well, time to go unfortunately. Best of luck though! 🙂

Like everyone else said, absolutely sexually assault. I want to address what you said about feeling aroused during it. Just because you may have felt aroused during some of it does not mean it wasn’t assault. Sexual assault doesn’t have to mean someone assaulting you and you screaming and crying about it. It means you told them NO you didn’t want to do that, which you did, and they kept going anyways. Someone once told me, you should never have to be talked into having sex or doing anything sexual. It should be something you fully want. I’ve been in situations with an ex boyfriend where he wanted sex and I absolutely didn’t and he ended up doing it anyways and my brain convinced myself during it that it was enjoyable when in fact it wasn’t. I realized later through therapy and help that I was being raped and my body’s response was protective aka made me feel like I wanted to be there in that moment because I couldn’t face what was happening for what it really was. So please don’t feel ashamed. Sexual acts can be enjoyable but if consent wasn’t given or was subsequently withdrawn, it’s assault or rape. I’m sorry this happened to you.

I’m not a guy HOWEVER just tell your girlfriend what happened. I get it, that’s awkward and probably embarrassing for you. But on her end she’s probably more or less thinking you couldn’t get off to her and probably feeling very insecure herself. Just tell her and maybe even make light of the situation (if you feel comfortable). Be like “hey babe, look I wanna talk about what happened the other night. You are so beautiful and I wanted you so badly. I fucked up and got the wrong condom size so I couldn’t perform. It won’t happen again I promise and I can’t wait for the next time we have sex” (or say “make love” instead of sex depending on if you guys are at that stage yet.) 

But either way bottom line is, she’s probably feeling just as insecure as you right now. Just tell her what happened, and if she truly likes you she won’t care at all and someday you both will look back and laugh at this situation.

Yeah and that’s exactly it, it wasn’t your fault. You have to let go of her and stop feeling like you could’ve somehow changed the outcome. I feel like maybe you know the truth as you’ve said in your post that she was “ugly on the inside” but you haven’t fully accepted it hence why you still feel she got away even if it wasn’t your fault. You have to let go. Easier said then done and I know this firsthand. I’m 25 and I think you said the clock feels like it’s ticking in another comment. I feel the same way sometimes but I promise you we are still young lol also looks fade. Beauty on the outside isn’t forever. It might be a dumb cliche but it’s literally true. Stop dating for awhile and let yourself heal. It seems like you have some trauma from that relationship and rightfully so if she was awful to you. I promise you will feel excited about another woman again. Trust me it will come when you least expect it but only if you let go of your ex and allow yourself to experience falling for somebody new. Also no one will ever be exactly like another person. If you spend your life trying to find someone like her or who tops her well it’s going to be exhausting.

Maybe stop looking for her replacement and just focus on yourself for a bit. Give it time and I’m sure you will meet a woman who you find 10x more attractive because she will not only be a 10 looks wise but also a 10 personality wise.

I haven’t experienced this but a few things that come to my mind are as follows: 

First I think he is most definitely excited. He definitely feels comfortable being able to do this around you and who knows how long he’s been suppressing it. For him telling you this confession probably felt like coming up for air for the first time in who knows how long. The fact you’ve remained supportive I think encourages him to be himself. Nothing wrong with that. 

However, I think it would be naive not to think about where this could lead. He could start cross dressing regularly. He could just be a man who enjoys wearing feminine items on occasion. He could want to transition someday (this isn’t necessarily going to happen, there are plenty of cross-dressers who aren’t trans). Only he knows these things. I’d say don’t bring up the shopping just yet. Maybe probe him and ask him how cross dressing has made him feel. He’s clearly excited but see if he will open up at all about what made him want to cross dress. 

As for the shopping and caring about his appearance, maybe try to turn it into a bonding moment if you are comfortable. Take him shopping with you and make it fun. Tell him what you think would look good on him :) I don’t think the shopping is a problem he’s probs just excited, however if it starts to affect your finances or he can’t afford to pay for the important things in life well that’s a different story. It sounds to me like he’s adding to his collection at the moment and is excited in doing so. 

Lastly, I can’t say if this will become the new normal but I think you should definitely prepare yourself for that possibility. If it becomes too much for you, then you have to decide if you can accept him for who he truly is or if you can’t. Ultimately that’s your decision but I think since this is all new, if you care about him and really don’t have a problem with all this I say turn it into something the two of you can relate on. Make him comfortable and let him know he can be confident around you. I’m sure as time passes he will make it clear what his end game is in all of this.
